King James Versus LeBron

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In a Carte Blanche exclusive we investigate who owns the king james trademark in South Africa, this after superstar basketball player is suing a local businessman.

Unique Selling Point:
Lebron James is a millionaire basketball player. He has changed his name many times, but most recently changed it to King James. Nike and LeBron wanted to follow in Michael Jordon's shoes literally and want to create the "king james shoe brand" and want it to go world-wide. Meanwhile in South Africa, former professional fighter James Thomson had retired after 18 year career in kick boxing/ muay-thai/MMA. He represented South Africa and was an international fighter. His ring name was ‘King James’. His career started in 1998 and ended in 2016. He is James Thomson the 4th of Scottish Highlander descent. He trademarked the King James name in South Africa in 2015 has a website selling apparel since 2004. His ‘King James’ trademark in South Africa is for apparel. And he knew nothing about Lebron James at that time or his ambition to register his trademark in South Africa.

Summary:
Then in the first quarter of 2018, a law firm in Pretoria retained by Lebron James contacted James out the blue and threatened him with litigation accusing him of bad faith. "They were after my ‘King James’ trademark for apparel in South Africa. Lebron James has a lifetime deal with Nike. He currently sells sneakers and apparel under the ‘Lebron’ name." Despite thomson explaining to lebrons attorneys that he had it legally, they decided to sue him anyway. Affidavits and heads of arguments have been submitted and the court case has since dragged out - they have been waiting for a court date since 2018. And thomson has paid R250,000 in legal fees already. Lebron's legal team to add insult to injury are dragging out the case for 3.5 years, hoping thomson will run out of money. They offered him just R5000 for the trademark.

Script:


Boxer and Muay Thai fighter James Thomson competed for 18 years. He was very good - a world title contender - and he called himself King James.
I adopted the King James ring name based upon the fact that our family's from Scottish highlander descent. My father's name is James midford Thompson my grandfather's name is James William Thompson, and it resonated with me.
He retired from the ring with four titles in a professional career spanning nearly two decades... Now he's a businessman with an impressive property portfolio.
Now living in East London, he has a new title: family man. Ten years ago he started selling athletic apparel under his King James ring name.
Being a businessperson I thought well let me trade mark it for apparel. I Started working on the King James brand and that's what I enjoy the most and it was something I was going to build on over a lifetime.
LINK: AND THEN IN APRIL 2018 THOMSON RECEIVED A LEGAL LETTER CLAIMING THE TRADE MARK KING JAMES BELONGED TO SOMEONE ELSE – AMERICAN BASKETBALL SUPERSTAR LEBRON JAMES.
LeBron James, from the US state of Ohio, has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat, and most recently The LA Lakers. A living basketball legend who’s also renowned for his fashion sense.
Upsounds: “I take fashion very seriously...
In 2018, three years after trademarking his brand name, Thompson got a call from his attorney with a question marking the beginning of this David versus Goliath tussle: “Have you heard of the basketball player, Lebron James? Because, you’ve got mail!
In a nutshell, the email said, LeBron James is a big shot, you're not as big a shot. Your brand's gonna dilute his brand. You got to scrap your trademark, scrap your domain, scrap your business or we're going to litigate you...
LEBRON JAMES HAS HAD MANY NICKNAMES THROUGHOUT THE YEARS: HE WAS KNOWN AS THE CHOSEN ONE, THE AKRON HAMMER, BRON BRON, THE L TRAIN TO NAME A FEW, BUT IN HIS PAPERS THEY ALLEGE HE’S ALWAYS BEEN KNOWN AS KING JAMES.
LeBron is now 36 and - like most star athletes - is cashing in on his success.
THE GLOBAL LICENSED SPORTS MERCHANDISE MARKET IS WORTH OVER 26 BILLION US DOLLARS, WITH PREVIOUS BASKETBALL GREATS LIKE MICHAEL JORDON SHARING IN THAT WITH HIS AIR JORDAN SNEAKERS, LEBRON JAMES AND NIKE HAVE ALSO STRUCK A DEAL.
LeBrons shoes make 340 million dollars for Nike per year...while his sneakers average between R2,500 -R4,000 PER PAIR. According to the court papers, his interests are being represented by his American trademark company.
If they come to me said, Look, Mr. Thompson, Le Bron James got a lifetime deals gonna be worth $3 billion when he's finished branding his stuff King James, he needs your king james trademark in SA. Let's see what they want with the prepared offer us for this thing in a civil decent fashion.
Masa: That’s fair?
10.24 I've invested 10 years of my life in the hundreds of thousands of rands developing logos, pain designers, you know, so what is what is what is your offer on this test?
So what would this multimillion dollar sports and fashion empire put on the table through their local attorney? Well, the answer might surprise you.
So she says 5000 Maybe 8000 Rand
Masa: R5,000?
And then my switch was flipped, and I was like no fine and we will then go the court route.
And so a court will decide whether Thomson’s brand is worth roughly the same as two pairs of Lebron sneakers.
LINK: “WHAT'S IN A NAME? ASKED WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE? WELL FOR BOTH JAMES THOMSON AND LEBRON JAMES A LOT.
How could I possibly know back in the early 2000s that LeBron James was gonna rebrand himself King James and rebrand the sneaker? I'm not a scumbag. We're going to copy some other superior athletes trademark that is not my style.
Three years later, Thomson is down R250,000 in legal fees. Trademark law in South Africa is complex, so we asked WebberWentzel intellectual property partner, Bernadette Versfeld, for the simple version…
When you create your brand, that is when you want to apply for registration of your brand. Once your trademark is registered, then you will have statutory protection.
The trademark here applies to clothing, footwear and headgear. Trademarks are territorial, and Thomson owns the trademark only in South Africa.
Our trademarks Act protects foreign well-known trademarks. They don't need to have sold any products or offered any services in South Africa. So if LeBron James’ legal team can show that they have a that they trademark that King James is a well known trademark, prior to Thompson's application, then they could succeed.
LINK: THERE’S NO DOUBT THAT LEBRON IS A SUPERSTAR, BUT ONE OF THE KEY ISSUES AT THE CORE OF THIS CASE, WILL BE WHETHER SOUTH AFRICANS KNOW HIM AS KING JAMES.
In other words, Lebron’s legal team needs to prove that a specific sector of the public immediately links the name “LeBron” to the trademark “King James”.
You'd actually go to the relevant sector of the public: perhaps there are Basketball Association's or perhaps companies that sell sneakers.
Versfeld sets out LeBrons main legal points.
They argue Thomson wasn't the true owner of the trademark when he applied for it in 2015, adding that the registration and use of the trademark by Thompson is going to cause deception or confusion. They say THOMPSON was aware of LeBron James and his connection to the name King James, and only applied for the mark, because he sought his you know, big ticket to the money.
But Versfeld’s view is that Lebron's legal team hasn’t proven that
Thomson acted in bad faith.
WE WANTED TO ENSURE THAT LEBRON KNEW ABOUT THE LITIGATION IN SOUTH AFRICA AND DECIDED TO REACH OUT TO HIM ON SOCIAL MEDIA…
MASA LINK on twitter
Lebrons legal team declined the interview offer, saying; ‘Given the stage that the matter is in ...we are not in a position to discuss it at this time.’
I think it's a gamble. Because I don't think that they've LEBRONS LEGAL TEAM proved that the KING James Mark was well known in 2015.
Should the matter be settled, what is a trademark worth?
It's not a valuation of LeBron James's brand, the valuation that has to be done is a valuation of Thompson's brand. I don't think A seven digit number in dollars is fair. But I also don't think
R5000 or R10,000 is fair.
Going one-on-one with a global sports icon has taken more than just a financial toll on Thomson.
I don’t care about the money, i’ve got money. it's a situation where you find your wake up in the morning the night thinking of lebron James, you got to go to the toilet in the middle of night, Lebron James. Oh, my wife has had enough. You know, so it is immensely emotionally taxing.
For now, Thomson battles on, but the outcome of a legal tussle, 3 years in the running, is anything but a slam dunk.
